Crispy Chicken Schnitzel & Radicchio Salad Ingredients 2 thin chicken cutlets Salt + pepper 1/2 cup flour 2 eggs 1 cup breadcrumbs +sesame seeds for crunch Oil + 2 tbsp butter Salad Radicchio, fennel, red onion, apple or pear Dressing 4 tbsp olive oil 1 tbsp Dijon 1/2 a lemon 1 tbsp honey 1 garlic clove Salt + pepper Season chicken, dredge in flour, egg, then breadcrumbs and fry in oil + butter until golden and crispy. Toss salad ingredients together. Whisk dressing, toss with salad, and add some to the plate for the schnitzel!

The ice cream we got at home lol Cereal Milk Ice Cream 🍨🥣 4 cups milk 1 cup heavy cream 3 cups cornflakes or any cereal 2/3 cup sugar 1/4 teaspoon fine sea salt 5 egg yolks Toast the cereal in the oven at 300 degrees for 10 minutes, then pour warm milk over it and let steep for 20 minutes. Strain and heat the cereal milk with the heavy cream, half the sugar, and salt until steaming. In another bowl whisk the egg yolks with the remaining sugar, then slowly pour in the hot milk mixture while whisking. (This is called tempering the egg yolks) Return everything to the pot and cook on low, stirring constantly, until thickened enough to coat the back of a spoon. Strain and chill completely. (overnight if possible) Churn in an ice cream maker, ninja creami, etc. and freeze until scoopable. Cornflakes give you that nostalgic cereal milk flavor but you can do whatever!! Cinnamon Toast Crunch tastes almost like horchata, and Fruity Pebbles makes it extra sweet and colorful so have fun with it!

Let’s make Jollof Rice!  4 cups long-grain rice 2 red bell peppers 2 onions 2 scotch bonnet peppers/Habaneros 400g tomato paste 1 cup vegetable oil 1 tbsp ginger sliced 4 cloves garlic 4 cups chicken stock Fine sea salt to taste 1 tsp smoked paprika 1 tsp dried thyme 1 tsp dried rosemary 1 tsp garlic powder 1 tsp onion powder ½ tsp ground cumin ½ tsp ground coriander ½ tsp black pepper 4 bay leaves 2 tbsp butter Air fry or roast peppers, onions, garlic, and ginger at 350 Fahrenheit for 15–20 minutes, then blend smooth. Heat oil in a pot, sauté sliced onions until soft, then add tomato paste and cook it down on low until deep red and rich. Stir in the blended pepper mix, seasonings, stock, water and bay leaves, then cover and let it simmer for about 10 minutes. Add washed rice, stir gently, cover tightly, and cook on low, stirring once midway, until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Add butter, cover, and let it steam on low for 5 more minutes and enjoy!

Das coisas que mais AMO na cozinha é isso! Esses momentos de um trabalho “chato”, longo e repetitivo, em equipe. A gente se junta por um tempo e se foca só naquilo — e fala sobre tudo… sobre a vida, os problemas de cada um, as bênçãos, a felicidade, o ódio, o amor, o coração partido, o coração unido, quem a gente tá gostando no momento, quem a gente não tá gostando… A gente canta junto — uma música, duas ou três ao mesmo tempo — faz piada, dá risada, cria competição, brinca e sempre se acolhe. E assim vai. Quem conhece sabe: o querido confessionário da cozinha! Conforme a gente vai mudando de posição, vai deixando de fazer trabalhos como esse… então é sempre bom voltar e compartilhar esses momentos (meus preferidos). É a melhor parte de trabalhar em cozinha — as pessoas e suas histórias. Essas horas longas, dores e trabalhos massivos, quando compartilhadas com um sorriso no rosto, são a verdadeira poesia gastronômica. . . #fyppppppppppppppppppppppp #foryoupage #for #fyp #foodie

Ich weiß noch, wie sich bei den Beerdigungen meiner Eltern in mir alles dagegen sträubte, mich in die erste Reihe zu setzen. Dort zu sitzen machte es für mich real. Es machte es zu meinem Schicksal. 2023 war das schlimmste Jahr meines Lebens. Ich dachte, ich werde nie wieder glücklich. Als wäre ich in das Leben eines anderen verflucht worden. Ein schweres Schicksal folgte dem nächsten. Man sagt, die eigenen Eltern bereiten einen auf alles vor, nur nicht auf ihren eigenen Tod. Aber irgendwie haben meine mir trotzdem geholfen, diese Zeit zu überstehen. Sie wussten, dass ich das schaffe. Heute blicke ich auf das letzte Jahr zurück. Meine Eltern fehlen mir jeden Tag. Aber ich weiß, dass sie sich über meine Entwicklung freuen. Ich weiß, dass sie stolz auf uns sind. Und ich weiß auch: Ich habe es da rausgeschafft, weil sie mir geholfen haben, zu dem Menschen zu werden, der ich heute bin. Glücklich. #grievingjourney #trauer #griev

These little meringue chicks are bringing all the Easter sweetness 🐣💛 Light, airy, and almost too cute to eat, they’re the kind of treat that makes a spring table feel extra special. Perfect for Easter brunch, gifting, or making sweet memories in the kitchen with your littles. Meringue Chicks Recipe Ingredients: 	•	2 large egg whites, room temperature 	•	1/2 cup granulated sugar 	•	1/8 tsp cream of tartar 	•	1/2 tsp vanilla extract 	•	Yellow food coloring 	•	Orange decorating icing, orange candy melts, or orange gel icing for the beaks 	•	Black decorating gel or edible marker for the eyes Instructions: 	1.	Preheat oven to 200°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. 	2.	In a clean, dry mixing bowl, beat egg whites until foamy. Add cream of tartar and continue beating until soft peaks form. 	3.	Gradually add sugar, 1 tablespoon at a time, beating until stiff, glossy peaks form. Mix in vanilla extract. 	4.	Add a few drops of yellow food coloring and gently mix until the color is even. 	5.	Transfer the meringue to a piping bag. Pipe a larger round for the body, then a smaller round on top for the head to create chick shapes. 	6.	Bake for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until dry to the touch. Turn off the oven and let them cool inside with the door slightly cracked. 	7.	Once completely cool, add little eyes and orange beaks to bring your chicks to life. Tip: Meringue does best on a dry day, since humidity can make it sticky. #yum #recipe #easter #spring #modernprairie

We had never seen this before… and we couldn’t stop thinking about it 🌿 In Florida, we saw orchids that looked like they were on their last leg—gently wrapped onto palm trees… and somehow, they were thriving. Blooming. Coming back to life. It turns out, orchids don’t always need a pot or perfect conditions. In the wild, they grow on trees, not in soil—just holding on, finding what they need from the air, the light, and the environment around them. There was something so beautiful about that… a reminder that sometimes all we need is a different place to land. Not gone. Not finished. Just waiting for the right conditions to bloom again ✨ #saturday #spring #bloom #gardentok #modernprairie

Saturday’s project = pollinator gardens in the making 🌱🦋 We’re using leftover eggshells, a little soil, and hummingbird and butterfly-friendly seeds, then watering them daily on the windowsill until they’re ready for the outdoors. I love that this is such a simple way to reuse what we already have and create something beautiful with purpose. Pollinator gardens help support the butterflies, hummingbirds, bees, and other pollinators that need safe places to feed and thrive — and even the smallest garden can make a difference. Come spring, you’ll see the magic happen. ✨   One quick gardening note: eggshells can be a cute seed-starting holder, but they work best mainly as a reusable mini container; their calcium breaks down slowly, so the biggest benefit here is reusing a kitchen leftover while starting seeds in a fun way.  ##saturday##spring##gardentok##project##modernprairie

Honey 🍯 Glazed Salmon 🍣  Ingredients: 2 lbs salmon fillet 4 tbsp honey 3 tbsp soy sauce 4 garlic cloves, minced 1 tbsp lemon juice 1 tsp paprika Salt & black pepper to taste 1 tbsp olive oil Optional: red pepper flakes, sesame seeds, parsley Instructions: Pat salmon dry and season with salt, pepper, and paprika. Mix together: honey soy sauce garlic lemon juice Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat and sear salmon for about 2 minutes per side. Pour the glaze over the salmon. Cook for 10–15 minutes until tender and flaky. Pour the glaze over the salmon before serving. Tip: If you want the sauce extra sticky, simmer the leftover glaze in the pan for a few minutes until it thickens. Salmón 🍣 Glaseado Con Miel 🍯  Ingredientes 2 libras de salmón 4 cucharadas de miel 3 cucharadas de salsa de soya 4 dientes de ajo picados 1 cucharada de jugo de limón 1 cucharadita de paprika Sal y pimienta al gusto 1 cucharada de aceite de oliva Opcional: ají triturado, semillas de ajonjolí y perejil Seca el salmón y agrégale sal, pimienta y paprika. En un bowl mezcla: miel salsa de soya ajo jugo de limón Calienta el aceite de oliva en un sartén y sella el salmón por 2 minutos de cada lado. Agrega la salsa de miel encima del salmón. Cocina por 10–15 minutos hasta que esté suave y jugoso. Báñalo con más salsa antes de servir. Combina Perfecto Con Arroz blanco Vegetales Tostones Puré de papas Aguacate 🥑 Tip Si quieres la salsa más espesa y pegajosa, deja cocinar el sobrante de la salsa en el sartén por 2–3 minutos más.

Rinder-Schmorbraten für 2 Personen🥩: 500 gr. Rinderbraten  500 gr. Drillinge 2 Karotten 2 Zwiebeln 2 Knoblauchzehen 2 EL Tomatenmark 2 EL Mehl 300 ml Traubensaft oder Rotwein 500 ml Rinderbrühe 1 EL Salz Pfeffer Paprikapulver Zubereitung: Rindfleisch trocken tupfen. Zwiebeln grob schneiden, Möhren schälen und vierteln, Kartoffeln gründlich waschen. In einem großen Schmortopf (ich hatte keinen, deswegen hab ich einen Glastopf benutzt) Butter erhitzen und das Fleisch rundherum kräftig anbraten. Danach herausnehmen. Zwiebeln und Knoblauch in der restlichen Butter 1–2 Minuten anbraten. Tomatenmark kurz mitrösten, mit Mehl bestäuben und mit Traubensaft ablöschen. Kurz einkochen lassen. Dann Rinderfond, Salz, Pfeffer, Paprikapulver und das Fleisch dazugeben. Alles zugedeckt ca. 3 Stunden sanft köcheln lassen. Zum Schluss das Fleisch mit zwei Gabeln zerpflücken. Guten Appetit!  #schmorbraten #rinderbraten

I was so thrilled when CARE contacted me a few weeks ago about reimagining a CARE PACKAGE® through miniature art to help spread the word that CARE PACKAGE is now available in the U.S. 🧡 At the time, I happened to be on those days of the month when all I wanted was pain relief and something sweet (iykyk 🍫). That inspired me to think: what if I saved a little extra for someone going through their period while unexpectedly away from home? Periods are such a natural part of life, yet period care is often a quiet and overlooked need. Being on your period is already hard enough. I can’t imagine going through it while also being away from home during a difficult moment caused by things like natural disasters or other unexpected situations. So this became my tiny contribution to CARE’s mission of helping communities in times of need. Inside this miniature CARE Package are: a MiniCare tampon pack, a tiny tissue box, a bottle of pain relief, an insulated water bottle, a little period tracker notebook and some bear-shaped chocolate for comfort. They may be tiny, but each piece was created with so much care and love. I’m truly honored to tinyly contribute to CARE and the incredible work they’ve been doing for nearly 80 years 🧡 Tiny acts of care can mean so much. If you'd like to support someone in need, consider sending a CARE PACKAGE and help spread a little comfort and care 🧡 #CAREPartner #MiniatureArt #CAREPACKAGE #PeriodCare

Hot vs. Cold Lobster Roll - Which is Better? 🦞🍞 RECIPES BELOW ⬇️  NOTE: I like to go for a 1/3 lb of cooked lobster per roll. You will need a 1 - 1.25 lb lobster to yield that amount of meat. For instructions on how to cook lobster - check out my video linked below where I demonstrate how:  MAINE-STYLE ROLL: 👉 Mix 1/3 lb of lobster meat cut into 1/2” chunks with 2 tbsp mayo, 2 tbsp diced celery, a small squeeze of lemon, and a pinch of old bay. Season with sea salt to taste. I like to garnish my roll with some of the paler-green celery leaves from the inside of the celery head.  CONNECTICUT-STYLE ROLL: 👉 Gently heat up 1/3 lb of lobster meat cut into 1/2” chunks in a 1/4 cup of melted butter (ideally clarified). Keep the pot over low heat, and ensure it doesn’t boil. Remove the lobster from the pot with a slotted spoon, and add it to a mixing bowl with a generous pinch of chopped chives. Season with sea salt and lemon juice to taste.  BROWN BUTTER HOLLANDAISE ROLL: (this will make enough hollandaise for 3-4 rolls…) 👉 brown 1/4 lb of butter in a sauce pot, and allow to cool to between 55-60 degrees Celsius. Add two egg yolks and the juice from half a small lemon to a container, and slowly start to emulsify in your brown butter with an immersion blender. Continue adding more butter until your hollandaise has thickened, and can coat the back of a spoon. Season with sea salt to taste. Warm your lobster gently in the microwave (30 seconds max), and toss with your hollandaise and a pinch of chives.  #lobster #roll #lobsterroll #homecooking #recipe

How to Cook & Break Down Lobster 🦞🦞 - BASICS WITH BEN FULL INSTRUCTIONS BELOW ⬇️  1. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. You want enough water in the pot to fully submerge each lobster. When salting your water, use sea salt (quite generously), until your water tastes like the sea.  2. Cook your lobster 7 minutes for the first lb + 3 minutes for each subsequent 1/2 lb. My lobsters were each 1.75 lbs, so that meant 11.5 minutes. HOWEVER - this cooking time starts once your water comes back up to a boil, after you put your lobsters in. It took about 90 seconds for my water to come back up to a boil after adding my lobsters, so total cook time was approx. 13 minutes.  3. While your lobster is cooking, prepare a large ice bath (or multiple ice baths). When your timer goes off, plunge your lobster into the ice water to shock them and stop the cooking. Allow your lobster to fully cool in the ice water. 4. Remove your lobster from the ice water, and try to drain off as much excess water as possible. Grab the lobster by the body with one hand, and twist off the tail, legs, and claws (from the base of the knuckles).  5. Starting with the tail, firmly press down on the side of the tail with the palm of your hand until you hear a crack. From here, you will see the crack running down the underside of the tail. Open the crack as wide as you can, and pull out the tail. Looking into the opening of the tail from the thickest point (where the tail was attached to the body), you will see the brown digestive tract. Pull it out as best you can with tweezers, and run cold water into the cavity to clean out whatever is remaining.  6. For the knuckles, you will see three distinct segments. Cut off the smallest segment with scissors. Then use your scissors to cut the shell along opposite sides of the knuckle, being careful not to pierce the meat. From here, you can simply remove the shell and extract the meat.  7. For the claws, push the "thumb" (I don’t know what the technical term is for it… 😅) back and forth until it is loose. Then pull it directly outwards, hopefully pulling out a large piece of cartilage with it. If the cartilage doesn’t come out, you must cut it out of the claw later. Next, using a heavy chefs knife, use the butt of the knife to crack the shell of the claw at the widest point. Give a few swift shots with your knife as needed until the shell breaks in half. (see video for reference). From here you can pull out the claw meat.  8. Lastly, for the legs (if you want to go the extra mile), use a rolling pin to push out the meat like a tube of toothpaste.  9. Before serving, it is a good idea to rinse your lobster meat in ice water to remove any shell fragments, as well as any of the white paste that might be visible on the meat.  #lobster #instructions #cooking #homecooking #recipe

How to Make a Créme Caramel 🍮🍮 - FRENCH CLASSICS 🇫🇷 FULL RECIPE BELOW ⬇️  NOTE: This recipe is for a 9" wide pie dish that is 1.5" deep. If using another mould, quantities must be scaled accordingly! INGREDIENTS: 3 cups milk 1.5 cups whipping cream 1 vanilla pod 1/4 cup room temperature water 1.5 cups sugar 1/2 cup maple syrup 6 whole eggs 3 egg yolks Fleur de sel (to finish) INSTRUCTIONS: 1. Pre-heat your oven to 300 degrees Fahrenheit. You can also start a pot with 2-3 litres of hot water, to heat over low heat.  2. Add your milk and cream to a medium sauce pot. Cut your vanilla pod in half lengthwise, and scrape out the seeds. Add both the seeds and the pod to the your milk/cream mixture. Bring everything to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then immediately turn off the heat.  3. Add your whole eggs and yolks to a large heat-proof bowl, and whisk them until homogeneous with a 1/2 cup each of sugar and maple syrup.  4. Once your milk-cream mixture is hot, remove the vanilla pod, and start pouring it into your egg mixture, slowly at first, whisking vigorously as you go. Once half the milk/cream has been poured in, you can pour the rest relatively quickly. Set this mixture to the side for the moment. This is your custard base. 5. In a medium heavy-bottom pot or pan, add your remaining sugar (1 cup), along with your 1/4 cup of water. MAKE SURE your pot/pan is clean beforehand. Start the pan over medium heat, and watch as your sugar turns into a liquid syrup. From here, DO NOT stir your syrup, just till the pan if needed, or use a clean wet brush to brush down the walls of the pot/pan, if you see the syrup start to stick/crystallize. You are looking for a nice amber colour - but you will likely need to take the caramel off the heat BEFORE the entire caramel is amber in colour. Once approximately half the syrup reaches this colour, you can remove the caramel to continue cooking off the heat. If needed, you can always put your caramel back on the heat to get more colour - but you can’t fix a burnt caramel that is left on the heat too long! If you start to see smoke, that is the first sign to remove your caramel from the heat. This is not necessarily a bad thing - I find the first sign of smoke to be the perfect time to remove my caramel! Too much smoke however is a very bad sign.  6. Once your caramel is ready, pour it in your baking dish. Next, use a strainer to pour your custard base into the baking dish over the caramel. From here, place your baking dish into a larger baking dish, that is large enough to comfortably fit your crème caramel. Transfer this set-up into the oven, then fill the larger baking dish with hot water until it reaches ~1/2 way up the sides of your crème caramel dish. This is your "Bain-Marie", which will allow your flan to cook slowly and evenly.  7. Cook your flan for 45-60 minutes, or until the inner 75% of the custard jiggles (but does not look wavy/liquidy). You can also test by inserting a cake tester into the middle of the custard, and ensuring it comes out clean. My custard took 55 minutes, but this will vary depending on the strength of your oven, and the ingredients you are using.  8. Allow your custard to cool in the fridge for at least 6 hours, but ideally overnight. When ready to serve, release the crème caramel from the sides of your baking dish using an offset spatula, or another thin tool. Invert your flan onto a large plate, slice, and serve! Finish with fleur de sel, and a generous drizzle of caramel. Enjoy! #cremecaramel #flan #french #homecooking #recipe

How to Make Wild Garlic Pesto 🍃🌱 (Ramp Pesto) - BASICS WITH BEN FULL RECIPE BELOW ⬇️  INGREDIENTS: - 2L fresh ramp leaves (loosely packed) - 1L fresh basil leaves (loosely packed) (Contrary to what I said in the video, I still like to add a little bit of basil to my ramp pesto! However, you can still do 100% ramps get an excellent result, just replace the basil leaves for more ramp leaves in this recipe) - 75g freshly grated Parmesan cheese - 1/2 cup pine nuts - 1/2 cup olive oil + more as needed  - 1 lemon - 1 clove garlic - freshly cracked black pepper (to taste) - salt (to taste) INSTRUCTIONS:  1. Blanch your ramps (and basil, if using) for 5-10s in heavily salted boiling water, then immediately shock in ice water. Once cooled, squeeze as much water out of your leaves as possible. 2. Toast your pine nuts over medium heat until they’re slightly golden. 3. Add blanched/squeezed greens, toasted pine nuts, 1/2 cup olive oil, 1 clove grated garlic, grated Parmesan, zest + juice from 1 lemon to a blender, and blend until smooth. Add more olive oil as needed while blending until the pesto is smooth & creamy. If your blender (and pesto) starts getting too warm, add an ice cube or two to cool it down. 4. Season your pesto with salt, and freshly cracked black pepper to taste. Enjoy!  NOTE: This recipe works for many leafy greens & herbs! Arugula, kale, spinach, mint, parsley… you can play around with different combinations depending on what’s in season, and this process will always yield a great result! #pesto #ramps #wildgarlic #homecooking #recipe

How to Make Strawberry Rhubarb Crisp 🍓🌱 - Will it Tarte Tatin ep. 9 - RHUBARB  INGREDIENTS: 2 cups strawberries (halved) 2 cups rhubarb (cut into 1 cm segments) 1/3 cup granulated sugar 1/4 cup strawberry jam 1.25 cups flour 1 cup instant oats 3/4 cup softened butter 3/4 cup brown sugar INSTRUCTIONS: 1. Pre-heat your oven at 375 degrees Fahrenheit. 2. Chop your strawberries and rhubarb into roughly the same size pieces. Toss both in your granulated sugar. 3. In a large pan, heat your strawberry jam until liquified. Remove from the heat, and mix in your strawberries and rhubarb. Divide your fruit mix between 4 small ramekins or gratin dishes (oven safe). 4. Mix your softened butter, flour, brown sugar and oats, until it has the texture of damp sand. It is okay for there to be small clumps! This will result in a better final texture.  5. Spread your crumble mixture around the top of your fruit, piling on as much as possible, pressing it down gently. You will have a lot of crumble - but try your best to get it all on your fruit! The strawberry/rhubarb mixture will shrink/reduce while baking, so you need much more than you think!  6. Transfer your baking dishes onto a baking tray (this is VERY necessary, as liquid will spill over while baking), and bake for 30-45 minutes, or until any visible liquid has reduced to a thick, syrupy consistency, and your crumble is golden brown.  7. Let rest for 10-15 minutes before serving for best results. Serve with a generous scoop of vanilla ice cream, and enjoy!  #strawberry #rhubarb #crisp #homecooking #recipe

How to Male Uni Carbonara 💥💥 FULL RECIPE BELOW ⬇️  (feeds 2 people)  INGREDIENTS: 8-10 whole sea urchin (in shell)  OR  160-200g cleaned uni (120-160g for sauce + 40g for garnish)  6 egg yolks 250g spaghetti 1/4 bunch chives 1 lemon 2 tbsp unsalted butter fine sea salt (to taste) INSTRUCTIONS:  1. If using whole urchin, process your urchin as demonstrated in this video: https://vt.tiktok.com/ZS9bEx1SU/ 2. Set aside your two nicest uni for presentation (to add fresh on top of your pasta). If using pre-processed uni, you can typically buy two different grades; pristine/grade-A uni, and uni that is discoloured, or was damaged while processing. The damaged/discoloured uni is cheaper, and perfect for your sauce. Fish markets will typically sell this kind of uni expressly for the purpose of cooking.  3. With your less-nice uni, combine them in a blender with your egg yolks. You’re looking for equal parts yolks and uni. Generally, a whole uni will weigh 15-20 grams and so does a large egg yolk. Counting 1:1 will generally yield a good result. Blend until smooth.  4. Bring a large pot of heavily salted water to a boil. Cook your pasta as per package instructions. With 2-3 minutes left in the cook time, add 1/4 cup of your pasta water to a large, heavy-bottom pan over very low heat. Whisk in your butter until emulsified. Add your egg/urchin mix, and continue to stir over very low heat. Add your pasta directly from the pot to the pan, trying to shake off as much excess pasta water as possible.  5. Toss your pasta in the sauce over low heat until the sauce can cling to the noodles. Add extra pasta water as needed. Finish your pasta with a squeeze of lemon juice, and adjust seasoning with salt to taste.  6. Plate up your pasta, and garnish with finely chopped chives, and your nicest uni on top. Enjoy!  #uni #urchin #seaurchin #carbonara #recipe

How to Blanch Vegetables 🥦🫛🌱 - BASICS WITH BEN FULL INSTRUCTIONS ⬇️ 1. CLEAN/PREP YOUR VEG AHEAD OF TIME. Once you start blanching, you want to be focusing on your veggies - they can go from perfectly cooked to overcooked in a few seconds. They need your full, undivided attention! Because of this, make sure all your veggies are lined up and ready to go. Some examples of prepping your veg include removing the thick, woody end from asparagus, or removing the fibrous "spine" from your snap peas.  2. MAKE SURE YOU HAVE A LOT OF ICE. When shocking your vegetables in ice water, you want to cool them down as quickly as possible, effectively stopping the cooking ASAP. If you do not have enough ice in your water, this will be made more difficult! Be sure to have plenty of ice on hand before starting.  3. USE A LARGE POT. Thomas Keller likes to call this method "big pot blanching", because the bigger the pot, the easier it is to keep your water boiling, and thus, the easier it is to blanch your vegetables quickly, keeping them nice and vibrant. You are looking to add your vegetables to the pot without the water stopping boiling. If you don’t have a pot large enough, you can also add less vegetables at once, effectively preventing the water from stopping boiling as well.  4. HEAVILY SALT YOUR WATER: You want your water to be quite salty - tasting just like the ocean. Technically speaking, you’re looking at a ~4% salt solution. While this might seem excessive, your vegetables will only be in the water for a matter of seconds, and thus, won’t end up "overly salty". Once they are cooled down, you will find them to be perfectly seasoned.  5. PROPERLY COOL YOUR VEGETABLES. Once you plunge your vegetables into your ice bath, make sure they aren’t clumped together. You can agitate them if needed to make sure they are all in contact with a steady flow of cold water. Do not take out your veggies until they are fully cooled down. For larger veggies, this might require you to cut into a piece to ensure it is cooled down internally. However, do not leave your vegetables in the ice water for too long, as they will become water-logged.  6. PROPERLY STORE YOUR VEGGIES. Once you have taken your vegetables out of the ice bath, take an extra moment to drain off any excess water, because if you immediately transfer soaking wet vegetables into a container, they will likely get soggy/deteriorate. Depending on the vegetable, a good quality paper towel at the bottom of your container can help absorb any excess water.  7. REHEATING YOUR VEGETABLES. While you can re-heat/serve your vegetables as you’d like. Just remember that your vegetables are (ideally) 90% cooked, and won’t need to be re-heated for very long. My favourite way to serve blanched green vegetables in particular, it to glaze them in stock and butter (approx 1:2 ratio), seasoned with salt, and a small squeeze of lemon juice at the end.  #blanch #blanching #vegetables #homecooking #recipe

How to Cook Fish pt.1 🐟🐠 (Using a Cake Tester) - BASICS WITH BEN There are a number of different ways to cook fish (pan searing, poaching, confit, broiled), but regardless of which method you use, you need to know when the fish is done! Regardless of how you’re cooking your fish, a cake tester will help you achieve the perfect doneness.  As I mentioned in the video, the best way to check if a fish is done, is to insert your cake tester against the grain of the fish, and when you are met with ZERO resistance, your fish is done. You are then going to check the temperature by feel, which should be pleasantly warm to the touch (42-45 degrees Celsius). However, there are a few caveats to note; 1. You must insert your cake tester directly into the middle of your fish, directly through the thickest part of your filet. Especially for thicker portions of fish, this is important to make sure the fish is cooked all the way through.  2. You need to check your fish semi-often, and identify the SOONEST POINT that the cake tester meets zero resistance. If your fish is 10 degrees overcooked, the cake tester will also meet zero resistance, but the temperature will be too high at that point. Because of this, it important to keep a close eye, and once again, confirm with the temperature of the fish, as soon as the cake tester pierces cleanly.  3. There are some fish that require higher cooking temperatures. While they aren’t as common, skate, swordfish, and some other varieties will require a temperature hotter than "warm". Know the fish you are cooking, and prepare accordingly! The cake tester will still be a useful tool, just with a different target temperature. For most common fish however (salmon, halibut, cod…) this method is ideal!  4. For the perfect flaky fish, be sure to rest your fish before eating it! Fish doesn’t require as long a rest as steak, but 4-5 minutes will go a long way in ensuring the ideal texture.  5. Also like a steak, tempering your fish for 15-20 mins at room temperature before cooking will allow it to cook more evenly! BONUS TIP: When poaching, confiting, or baking a fish where you won’t serving the skin, keep the skin on while you’re cooking the fish! The reason for this, is that when the skin peels off easily, also with zero resistance (noticing a trend here…? 😅), your fish is perfectly cooked! The skin will also keep the fish moist as it cooks.  #cooking #fish #caketester #homecooking #Recipe

I ikut this video, senang sangat nak faham @Dee 💓 Ingredients: 500g tepung faiza 7g instant yeast 10g salt 350ml air suam 200g  shredded cheese half block of cold butter (pls do more 😭💓) Steps: 1. Mix flour, yeast & salt together. 2. Masuk air suam, stir really well, it might seem dry at first but once everything is combined it will moisten up.  3. Letak cheese of your choice and mix again well. Cover and rest for 30 min. After 30 min grate the cold butter and fold it over 6 times. 4. Be gentle untuk stretch the dough and fold it over. Cover and rest in the fridge overnight. Esoknya: 1. Tepungkan tempat untuk shape the dough, including top of the dough and your hand.  2. Help the dough keluar dari bowl and shape into a rectangle.  3. Cut the dough half, & each half divided into 4, each 4 bahagi lagi kepada 3, total 12pcs. 4. gently twist macam dalam video.  5. Cover them and rest for 30 min.  6. Preheat oven to 230C and add a dish with water to the bottom of the oven to create steam.  7. Bake for 10 min, after 10 min take out the water.  8. Bake for another 10 min.  9. After 10 min terbalikkan stick and bake for 5-7 min until their golden. (Kalau nak simpan beku boleh skip this part, bila nak makan, thaw overnight dalam chiller & sambung step 9 ni) kene selalu tengok sbb takut hangus, sebab setiap size berbeza 💗

Ciabatta 🥖🍞 (untuk lebih faham 👇🏻) https://vt.tiktok.com/ZS9TLVtfC/ Ingredients:  - [ ] air suam 200ml - [ ] instant yeast 4g - [ ] olive oil 20ml - [ ] tepung roti 250g - [ ] garam 1/2 tbs Steps: 1. masukkan instant yeast dlm air suam, kacau rata. 2. masukkan olive oil, kacau lagi. 3. masukan tepung, kemudian garam, kacau rata sampai fully combined. 4. cover, & rest untuk 20 minutes. 5. basahkan tangan, stretch & fold 4 bahagian doh (setiap bahagian, basahkan tangan lagi dan lagi). 6. cover, & rest untuk 20 minutes. 7. ulang stretch & fold 4 bahagian doh.  8. angkat doh & terbalikkan upside down (dlm video saya tak buat sebab terlupa) 9. cover, & rest untuk 1 jam.  10. tabur tepung pd baking paper dan doh tadi. 11. terbalikkan doh pada baking paper, mcm dlm video. 12. tabur tepung atas permukaan doh & pisau atau cutter utk potong. 13. potong doh 2 bahagian. 14. cover & rest for 30 minutes dengan kain lembap. 15. panaskan oven 230C  16. bakar dengan small dish with water untuk create steam selama 10 minutes. 17. keluarkan air tadi & sambung bakar lagi 15minutes.  18. potong 2 bahagian, sapu butter (mcm dalam video), letak chicken mushroom, letak cheese, bakar sampai rangup/ cheese cair (230C dalam 5 minit) creamy chicken mushroom 🍄🍄‍🟫 Ingredients: - [ ] bawang putih - [ ] bawang holland - [ ] shitake mushroom - [ ] dada ayam - [ ] dried herbs (oregano, mix herbs or anything u have) - [ ] cooking cream (dalam video i pakai 2 kotak kecil) - [ ] cheese slice/ shredded cheese - [ ] daun ketumbar/ parsley - [ ] garam - [ ] cube pati ayam Steps: 1. racik bawang putih & bawang holland, tumis smpai wangi. 2. masuk sliced mushroom, tumis smpai layu, boleh letak air kalau terlampu kering supaya tak hangus. 3. masukkan dada ayam, cooking cream, cheese, garam, cube pati ayam smpai masak & kuah pekat. 4. masukkan daun ketumbar/ parsley. 😬

Let’s make Kaymak with Nana! Kaymak is similar to clotted cream, and we usually eat this creamy milk dish at breakfast paired with pastry puff (Kahi) and some type of sweet topping like honey. What you need: - A tray pan with large surface area. - 35% whipping cream Directions: -Add your carton of cream to your pan. Stir consistently on high heat until it reaches a boil. - lower the heat to 1 and let this sit for 2 hours on the stove. Do not move or mix. - After 1-2 hours once it thickens turn off the heat and let this cool completely. - Cover with a towel or paper towel. Do not let this touch the kaymak. Place in the fridge. - After 1-2 days in the fridge, your kaymak is ready! - Enjoy with bread or puff pastry and something sweet. Honey, Jam, or maple syrup. ✨Peach Cobbler Ninja Creami Dairy Free Ice Cream ✨ Ingredients: 2 cups frozen peaches ½ cup heavy coconut cream ½ cup sweetened condensed coconut milk 2 tbsp brown sugar 1 tsp vanilla extract tiny pinch salt ¼ tsp xanthan gum Crumble: ¼ cup rolled oats 2 tbsp brown sugar 1 tbsp flour 1 tbsp butter or vegan butter pinch cinnamon tiny pinch salt Instructions: -Add the peaches, coconut cream, condensed coconut milk, brown sugar, vanilla, salt, and xanthan gum to a Vitamix. -Blend until completely smooth and silky. -Taste the mixture before freezing and add more sweetness if needed. -Let the mixture sit a few minutes so air bubbles can settle. -Pour into a Ninja Creami pint and freeze for 24 hours. -Mix together the oats, brown sugar, flour, butter, cinnamon, and salt until crumbly. -Bake @ 400° (5-6 minutes) until golden brown and crisp. -Let the crumble cool completely. -Spin the Creami on the ice cream setting. -Add a splash of coconut cream and respin if needed. -Mix in the crumble.  #peachcobbler #icecream #ninjacreami #recipe #thrivemarketpartner

Replying to @heatco Me too! 👇🏼BUTTERSCOTCH COOKIES👇🏼 1/2 cup butter or margarine 2/3 cup brown sugar 1 egg 1 1/3 cups sifted all-purpose flour 3/4 teaspoon baking soda 3/4 teaspoon vanilla 1/3 cup chopped walnuts (I opted out of nuts, not a fan) Melt butter in 2-quart saucepan; add sugar and mix well. Add egg; beat till light colored. Sift flour with soda; stir into egg mixture. Add vanilla and nuts. Chill. Roll in small balls. Bake on ungreased cookie sheet at 375° for 8 to 10 minutes. Remove at once. Makes 3 dozen. #butterscotchcookies #baking #cookbook #series #Recipe

Mix thoroughly; shape in about 20 small balls and place in skillet. Mix remaining soup, water, and Worcestershire sauce; Pour over meatballs. 🍯 Comfort food… but with a little fire to it. 🌶️ I love taking familiar flavors and giving them a little edge, and this dish does exactly that. Rich, slow-braised short rib, creamy whipped potatoes with a garlicky Greek twist, crisp vegetables for balance, and then that hot honey chili crunch comes in and wakes everything up. For me, great food is all about contrast. Soft and crispy. Sweet and spicy. Comforting, but still exciting enough to keep you going back for another bite. This is the kind of dinner that feels cozy at first…  …until the heat sneaks up on you in the best possible way! Safe to say, this one doesn’t stay on the plate for long.  🔗 Be sure to try this dish of mine (and many more) on CookUnity by clicking the link in my bio! 🔗 🎥 Video by @juanch0pedia  🎬 Produced by @paulpilcz

🥙 You think you know Sabich? You haven’t had it like this. 🍆 Cooking this alongside @Chef Einat felt like stepping into a story. One where every layer has something to say. Crispy eggplant, jammy eggs, creamy tahini, bright pops of salad - it’s bold, it’s messy (in the best way), and it’s completely addictive. There’s tradition here, AND there’s personality. The kind of dish that invites you in, then keeps you coming back for just one more bite… and then one more… …and you guessed it - then one more. It’s vibrant, it’s soulful, and it’s meant to be eaten with your hands. No overthinking, just pure enjoyment. Tell us - who you’re sharing it with? 🎥 Video by @juanch0pedia  🎬 Produced by @paulpilcz  🧑‍🍳 Culinary Support by @BakedbyBiba

You haven’t lived if you haven’t had hummus like this. 💜 Roasted beets change everything. They bring this deep, natural sweetness and that unmistakable color. Something you don’t expect from a classic hummus, but immediately makes sense once you dig in it. I like to let the ingredients do the talking here. Nothing complicated. Just real balance.  Creamy, bright, a little earthy, a little sharp. The kind of dip that quietly steals the show without trying too hard. Swipe a crunchy pita chip through it, and you’ll get it. What kind of hummus do you want to see me make next? 🎥 Video by @juanch0pedia  🎬 Produced by @paulpilcz  🧑‍🍳 Culinary Support by @BakedbyBiba

If you love hummus - you need to try this 🥑 I love taking something classic and giving it a fresh, vibrant twist. This edamame and avocado hummus is exactly that.  It’s creamy, garlicky, and packed with flavor, but still feels light and bright.  I blend buttery avocado with tender edamame, a good hit of garlic, garlic oil, and citrus until it’s perfectly smooth and silky.  It’s the kind of dip that works for everything! Spoon it into a bowl for a crowd, spread it on sandwiches, or just grab some pita chips and dive in.  Simple, fresh, and always a hit! Have you tried a twist on hummus like this?
